### Front line

According to the Ukrainian open-source mapping project DeepStateMap, Russian forces occupied 5.4 km² of previously contested territory, while an additional 8.9 km² became newly contested, with 13% of the city of Kostiantynivka in Donetsk Oblast newly assessed as contested. Independent geolocation tracker GeoConfirmed verified multiple Russian drone strikes—specifically attributed to the "Rubicon" unit—targeting buildings and houses in Kostiantynivka. In contrast, the Russian Ministry of Defence (MoD) claimed that its Southern grouping of forces evacuated 16 civilians from Kostiantynivka, alleging Ukrainian drones attempted to disrupt the evacuation. 

Elsewhere along the front, the Russian MoD claimed its artillery struck Ukrainian strongpoints in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, strike drones targeted personnel in Sumy Oblast, and rocket artillery eliminated drone control sites on the Krasny Liman and Dnipropetrovsk axes. Meanwhile, GeoConfirmed geolocated Ukrainian artillery fire at several front-line points and recorded a Ukrainian airstrike against a prison facility in Mala Tokmachka, Zaporizhzhia Oblast. GeoConfirmed also noted a Russian uncrewed ground vehicle retrieving prisoners of war.

### Strikes and losses

The Ukrainian MoD claimed long-range overnight strikes targeted Russia's Subkhankulovo oil transfer station—a key hydrocarbon hub on the border of Bashkortostan and Tatarstan—and the Marinovka military airfield in Volgograd Oblast. GeoConfirmed verified footage and satellite imagery showing a burning fuel tank and heavy smoke at the Subkhankulovo station following a reported Ukrainian drone strike, and also recorded a Ukrainian attack drone heading toward the Slavyansk-on-Kuban oil refinery. The Russian MoD claimed its air defenses intercepted 343 Ukrainian drones overnight across multiple Russian regions (including Bashkortostan and Tatarstan) and an additional 34 drones during the day.

In Ukraine, the Russian MoD claimed it conducted strikes against defense industrial facilities in Kyiv, targeted a cargo vessel south of Odesa carrying alleged military cargo, and struck electrical substations in Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk, and Zhytomyr oblasts. GeoConfirmed reported Russian drone impacts on the "Avramivska" residential complex and the Lokomotiv Sports Palace in Kharkiv. GeoConfirmed also recorded potential war crimes, documenting three civilians wounded by Russian drone attacks in Zaporizhzhia, a civilian killed by a Russian drone, and an unverified drone drop targeting an individual and a dog.

Regarding equipment losses, GeoConfirmed recorded a Russian 2S19 Msta-S self-propelled howitzer destroyed by Ukrainian FPV drones. Open-source monitor WarSpotting located a destroyed Russian 2S19 Msta-S near Pisky in Kharkiv Oblast, whereas the Telegram channel *lost_warinua* separately claimed a destroyed Russian 2S19 was located near Peschanka in Russia's Belgorod Oblast.

### Official statements

The Ukrainian MoD announced regulatory reforms facilitating military education and rehabilitation for wounded soldiers, public university prep initiatives for veterans, defense AI integrations between Brave1 and Avengers Labs, and the presentation of Ukrainian defense technology at NATO Edge 26.

The Russian MoD reported on inaugural strategic consultations between Russian and Chinese defense officials in Beijing, highlighted a Collective Security Treaty Organization conference regarding military logistics, and publicized statements from captured Ukrainian soldiers claiming command neglect and severe supply shortages.
